originalTitle: SIF AUM jumps 29% to Rs 17,858 crore in June; inflows surge 171% MoM
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in simple terms: Specialised Investment Funds (SIF) had a big increase in the amount of money they manage, which went up by 29% to Rs 17,858 crore in June. This means more people are putting their money into these funds. The amount of new money coming into these funds also increased a lot, by 171%, compared to the previous month. This is a good sign for the overall mutual fund industry, which also saw many investors putting in money, especially through a regular investment plan called SIP. This shows that regular investors like you are continuing to invest in the stock market.

originalTitle: DMart Q1 results: Cons PAT up 11% to Rs 860 crore, revenue rises to Rs 18,795 crore
simplifiedContent: Avenue Supermarts, the company that owns DMart, has announced its financial results for the quarter ending June. The company's profit increased by 11.3% to Rs 860 crore, and its revenue (the amount of money it made from selling goods) rose by 14.9% to Rs 18,795 crore. This means the company made more money from sales than it did during the same time last year. The company's earnings before interest and taxes also grew by 15.4%, which is a good sign of its financial health. This increase in profit and revenue is a positive sign for the company's performance, which may be interesting to investors who own or are considering buying DMart's stock.

originalTitle: Nearly 60% of foreign inflows into India-focused funds withdrawn since 2024 peak: Report
simplifiedContent: Foreign investors have taken out almost 60% of the money they had put into funds that focus on India's stock market since the peak in 2024. This means they are moving their money to other investments, particularly those related to artificial intelligence around the world. In 2026, foreign investors pulled out $9 billion from India-focused funds. At the same time, some investors put money into US stocks and gold funds, and Europe also saw some new investment. This shift in investment matters because it can affect the overall performance of India's stock market.

originalTitle: Nomura sees 22% upside in Ather Energy. Here's why it's the brokerage's top EV pick
simplifiedContent: Nomura, a brokerage firm, thinks Ather Energy's stock price will go up by 22%. They are advising people to buy Ather Energy's stock because they believe the company will do well in the future. The reason for this is that more people are expected to switch to electric vehicles, and Ather Energy is likely to benefit from this change. Nomura has set a target price of ₹1,470 for Ather Energy's stock, which means they think it will reach this price due to its strong growth potential. This makes Ather Energy Nomura's top pick for electric vehicle companies.

originalTitle: Why large cap and mid cap funds could be the best mutual fund to bet on now, according to Abakkus study
simplifiedContent: A recent study by Abakkus Mutual Fund suggests that investing in large and mid-sized company funds could be a good idea right now. This is because the companies in these funds are seeing their earnings improve and their stock prices are at reasonable levels. A recent downturn in the market has created opportunities for long-term investors to get in at a good time. This means that the prices of these stocks might go up as the companies' earnings continue to grow. Overall, this could be a good time to invest in these types of funds for the long haul.

originalTitle: AI chip fever returns? SK Hynix  share price surges 13% after blockbuster $26.5 billion US listing
simplifiedContent: SK Hynix, a company that makes computer chips, just listed its shares on the US stock market and raised a huge amount of money, $26.5 billion. As a result, the company's share price jumped up by 13%. This is a big deal because it shows that investors are very interested in companies that make chips for artificial intelligence (AI). The strong demand for AI-related technology is driving up the price of these chips, which is good news for companies like SK Hynix. This surge in interest is happening despite some recent ups and downs in the market for semiconductor stocks.
